chunks: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: “For the mu'adhdhin, in what is between the adhan and the iqamah, is the like of the reward of the martyr who is drenched in his blood in the way of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.”
Then ʿAlī عليه السلام said: “They strive eagerly for the adhan.”
He said: “No. There will come upon the people a time when they will cast the adhan upon their weak ones; so those are flesh that Allah has forbidden to the Fire.”

key_terms.ضُعَفَائِهِمْ: their weak ones, upon whom people place the task
key_terms.ٱلشَّهِيدِ: the martyr slain in the way of Allah
key_terms.ٱلْإِقَامَةِ: the call signaling the commencement of prayer
key_terms.ٱلْمُؤَذِّنِ: the caller who gives the adhan for salat

ai.seo_question: What is the reward of the mu'adhdhin between the adhan and the iqamah?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the immense reward of the mu'adhdhin, likening it to the reward of a martyr in the path of Allah. It also foretells a time when people will neglect the honor of giving the adhan and leave it to the weak among them, while affirming the great merit and protection of such mu'adhdhins.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.869 - The Messenger of Allah (sw) said:
"The mu'adhdhin (caller to prayer) has a reward between the adhan and the iqamah equal to that of a martyr who is drenched in his blood in the way of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic."
Imam Ali (as) said: "People will compete over the adhan."
The Prophet replied: "No, there will come a time when people will leave the adhan to their weak ones. These (mu'adhdhins) are people whose flesh Allah (swt) has forbidden for the Fire”.
